name: finds a one-character chain while allowing an external target
input: classic intermediate dictionary words without the endpoint
test:
words = ['hot', 'dot', 'dog', 'lot', 'log']
assert transform_words('hit', 'cog', words, 1) is True
path = transform_words('hit', 'cog', words, 3)
assert path[0] == 'hit' and path[-1] == 'cog'
assert len(path) == 3
assert all(sum(left != right for left, right in zip(a, b)) in {1, 2} for a, b in zip(path, path[1:]))
assert all(word in words for word in path[1:-1])

name: keeps one- and two-character movement rules distinct
input: a two-character direct move to an external target
test:
assert transform_words('bake', 'bore', [], 1) is False
assert transform_words('bake', 'bore', [], 2) is True
assert transform_words('bake', 'torn', ['bore', 'tone'], 3) == ['bake', 'bore', 'torn']

name: handles endpoint, length, duplicate, and invalid-part boundaries
input: equal words, unequal endpoints, and duplicate dictionary entries
test:
assert transform_words('same', 'same', [], 1) is True
assert transform_words('same', 'same', [], 3) == ['same']
assert transform_words('a', 'bb', ['bb'], 1) is False
assert transform_words('a', 'bb', ['bb'], 3) == []
assert transform_words('ab', 'cd', ['ac', 'ac', 'zz'], 1) is False
try:
    transform_words('a', 'b', [], 4)
except ValueError:
    pass
else:
    raise AssertionError('invalid part should raise ValueError')
